thread: FOI 2026-024 — visor and lance from beneath the dining-room floor
subject: FOI Internal Review - 2026-024 - Great House Farm, Llandough
body:
Dear Mr Buckler

Thank you for your request for an internal review of Amgueddfa Cymru's response to your Freedom of Information request concerning a reported archaeological discovery at Great House Farm, Llandough.

I have now completed my review of the handling of your request, including the searches undertaken and the concerns raised in your request for review.

Having reviewed the original request, the searches conducted and the response provided, I am satisfied that the request was handled appropriately and that reasonable and proportionate searches were undertaken in those locations where information falling within the scope of the request would reasonably be expected to be held.

In your request for review, you suggest that additional searches should have been undertaken using a wider range of terms and concepts, including references to Roman burials, military burials, cavalry burials, human remains, horse remains and other archaeological terminology. I have carefully considered this point. However, when assessing whether information is held for the purposes of the Freedom of Information Act 2000, the relevant issue is not whether every conceivable search term has been used, but whether the authority has undertaken searches that are reasonable and proportionate in the circumstances and reasonably likely to identify relevant information if held.

Your request concerned a specific reported discovery at a named location. Accordingly, the location identified in the request was used as the primary search criterion. Searches were undertaken across Amgueddfa Cymru's information holdings where records relating to acquisitions, accessions, archaeological finds, provenance information and associated correspondence would reasonably be expected to be held. This included collections management systems, accession records, archived documentation, shared electronic records and other organisational record repositories.

Records identified through those searches were reviewed by collections staff and the FOI team to determine whether they related to the reported discovery described in your request. As the search methodology was location-based rather than focused on a particular object type, archaeological period or interpretation, it was reasonably likely of identifying relevant records regardless of whether associated material had been recorded as Roman, medieval or otherwise. I have therefore considered your suggestion that later historical accounts may have inaccurately described the nature, date or attribution of the reported discovery. I am satisfied that this possibility would not have affected the outcome of the searches undertaken.

I have also considered whether broader keyword searches would have been appropriate. Given the scale and diversity of Amgueddfa Cymru's collections and records, generic terms such as "horse", "burial" or "skeleton" would retrieve large volumes of records relating to many different sites and periods and would not provide a reliable or proportionate means of locating records relating to a specific reported discovery at a named location. I am satisfied that the location-based search strategy adopted was the most appropriate and proportionate approach.

The searches undertaken did not identify any records relating to:
* the acquisition, accession, donation, transfer or deposit of a visor, lance, helmet, armour or related objects associated with the discovery described in your request;
* associated human or animal remains connected with that discovery;
* reburial records relating to that discovery; or
* excavation reports, discovery reports or watching-brief records relating to the discovery described in your request.

Having reviewed both the scope of the original request and the searches undertaken, I am satisfied on the balance of probabilities that, if information relating to the reported discovery were held by Amgueddfa Cymru, those searches would have been likely to identify it.

You also raised concerns regarding the reference in the original response to other archaeological records identified during the course of the searches. Those records were reviewed and were not considered to relate to, or otherwise be associated with, the reported discovery described in your request. However, I can confirm that this aspect has been subject to further consideration and a separate response will be issued in relation to those records.

I therefore uphold the original conclusion that Amgueddfa Cymru does not hold recorded information falling within the scope of your request.

This concludes Amgueddfa Cymru's internal review process. If you remain dissatisfied, you may complain to the Information Commissioner's Office under section 50 of the Freedom of Information Act 2000.

Cofion cynnes,

FOI Team
foi.requests @museumwales.ac.uk
amgueddfa.cymru | museum.wales

Rhif elusen | Charity number 525774

thread: FOI 2026-032 — other archaeological discoveries at Great House Farm and Church Farm
subject: FOI - 2026-032 - Great House Farm, Llandough
attachments: FOI 2026-032 - 1924.jpeg; FOI 2026-032 - burial data.pdf; FOI 2026-032 - Filling the gaps.pdf; FOI 2026-032 - Llandough excavation.pdf; FOI 2026-032 - PAS finds.pdf; FOI 2026-032 - Roman Villa LLandough.pdf; FOI 2026-032 - Timeline Doc by Sion Bucklet.pdf; Llandough 82-44H details.xlsx; Llandough 95-56H details.xlsx; FOI - 2026-032 - explanatory doc.docx; Llandough 95-56H list.xls; Llandough 82.44H list.xls
note: FOI 2026-032 was registered by the Museum from the family's internal-review email of 26 August 2026 (transcribed under FOI 2026-024 above).
body:
Dear Mr Buckler

Thank you for your request for information, registered as FOI 2026-032.

As explained in our previous correspondence, this request has been considered separately from the internal review relating to FOI 2026-024.

We have identified a number of records relating to archaeological discoveries recorded at Great House Farm and Church Farm, both at Llandough. These records were identified during searches undertaken in connection with the earlier request but were not considered to fall within the scope of that request, which concerned a specific reported discovery.

We have now reviewed those records for the purposes of your new request.

Attached are copies of the relevant records. Certain information has been redacted from the disclosed records under section 40(2) of the Freedom of Information Act 2000, where it comprises the personal data of third parties. Disclosure of that information would contravene the data protection principles set out in UK data protection legislation.

To assist interpretation, we have also included a brief descriptor for each record, together with any available reference or catalogue information held within the Museum's records.

Further to these documents, we have also identified some publicly available records which I have referenced below.

An Early-medieval Monastic Cemetery at Llandough, Glamorgan: Excavations in 1994: Medieval Archaeology: Vol 49 , No 1 - Get Access<https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/epdf/10.1179/007660905x54044?needAccess=true>

Highlight 5: Llandough early medieval cemetery, Glamorgan (1994) - Cotswold Archaeology<https://cotswoldarchaeology.co.uk/highlight-5-llandough-early-medieval-cemetery-glamorgan-1994/>

Please note that the provision of these records should not be taken as indicating any association between them and the discovery you have described in FOI 2026-024. The records are being disclosed in response to your separate request for information relating to other archaeological discoveries recorded at the site.

If you are dissatisfied with the handling of this request, you may request an internal review within 40 working days of this response.

Cofion cynnes,

FOI Team
foi.requests @museumwales.ac.uk
amgueddfa.cymru | museum.wales

thread: FOI 2026-032 — other archaeological discoveries at Great House Farm and Church Farm
subject: RE: FOI - 2026-032 - Great House Farm, Llandough
body:
Dear FOI Team,

FOI 2026-032

Diolch yn fawr. Thank you for the records, the descriptors and the published references. This is a thorough response and it is genuinely useful.

One correction of place is required.

The request concerns Great House Farm (Tŷ Mawr), Llandough near Penarth / Cardiff. Among the disclosed PAS material is at least one record for a different property of the same name: Great House Farm, Llandough near Cowbridge (including 2022.18.1, NGR SS9934672805, medieval lead Romanesque mount). There is also a Great House farm entry at Llandow. Those are not the site named in the request. Two Llandoughs, and more than one Great House Farm, sit in the same county. The homonym is easy to miss and material.

Please treat the Cowbridge / Llandow entries as out of scope for this request unless you hold recorded information showing they were, at any time, indexed, cited, or treated as if they related to Great House Farm, Llandough (Penarth / Cardiff). If any such cross-attribution exists in historic files, catalogues, correspondence, or search notes, that recorded information is within scope and I ask that it be disclosed.

If labels or findspot fields are now amended to distinguish the two farms, please do not overwrite the original wording without retaining the prior form. I ask that any correction be recorded as a dated amendment, with the earlier descriptor preserved, so the sequence of how the records stood when searches were first run remains inspectable. Please do not destroy, weed, or replace the versions as disclosed on 22 September 2026.

One small point from my email of 26 August also remains. As item 7 I asked for any recorded information showing the basis on which the Museum concluded that the identified records were unrelated to the reported nineteenth-century discovery. If that conclusion was reached by staff judgement and not written down, please simply confirm that no recorded information is held on that point. I am not asking for a new opinion.

Could you also confirm the date by which you expect to respond to FOI 2026-036?

Cofion,

Sion Buckler
greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com

thread: FOI 2026-032 — other archaeological discoveries at Great House Farm and Church Farm
subject: RE: FOI - 2026-032 - Great House Farm, Llandough
body:
Mr Buckler

Thank you for your email.

Just to clarify, our collections management system records items individually and does not group records together based on similar place names. We are not aware of any recorded information showing that records for Great House Farm, Llandough (near Cowbridge) or Great House Farm, Llandow were ever catalogued or treated within the collections system as relating to Great House Farm, Llandough (near Penarth/Cardiff). The references to similarly named locations arose from our searches for information relevant to your request, rather than from any overlap within the collections records themselves.

In relation to item 7 of your email of 26 August, we do not hold any separate recorded information explaining the basis on which staff concluded that the identified records were unrelated to the reported nineteenth-century discovery. That conclusion was reached through staff assessment of the available records, and no further recorded information is held.

I hope this helps clarify our position.

Cofion cynnes,

FOI Team
foi.requests @museumwales.ac.uk
amgueddfa.cymru | museum.wales
